# Census Data

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
#Load Packages 
library(sf)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidycensus)
library(tidygeocoder)
library(flextable)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(tmap)
library(terra)
```

## 1) Use the tidycensus package to download American Community Survey five-year estimates from 2019-2023 in California at the County level for the following variable, including spatial data: a.) Household Median Income = “B19013_001”

```{r q1chunk2, echo = FALSE}
#ACS Data-setfrom 2019-2023 w/ spatial features
#The "geometry = TRUE" imports spatial features. 
ca.tracts <- get_acs(geography = "tract", 
              year = 2023,
              variables = c(medinc = "B19013_001"),
              state = "CA",
              output = "wide",
              survey = "acs5",
              geometry = TRUE,
              cb = FALSE)
ca.tracts

#Organize/Separate the "NAME" column 
ca.tracts <- ca.tracts %>%
             separate(NAME, c("Tract", "County", "State"), 
                       sep = "; ")

```

## 2) Take a glimpse at your data.

```{r q2chunk3}
#Glimpse at data set w/ "NAME" column separated & joined files 

glimpse(ca.tracts)

```

## 3) Make a map of median income by County.

```{r q3chunk4}

tmap_mode("plot") #Best tmap mode for knitting file 

tract_map <- tm_shape(ca.tracts) +   tm_polygons()

tract_map
```

## 4) Now can you change the color palette?

```{r q4chunk5}

#Changed the tracts to be a green color scheme 
tm_shape(ca.tracts) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "medincE", 
  fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(style = "quantile", n=4, values = "Greens"))
```

## 5) Can you add a nice title and add a legend?

```{r, echo=FALSE, q5chunk6 }
tm_shape(ca.tracts) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "medincE", 
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(style = "quantile",n=4,
                                              values = "brewer.greens"),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Median Income")) + 
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE, legend.outside.position = "right") +
  tm_title(text = "Median Income of CA Tracts",
           size = 1.25, 
           position = tm_pos_out("center","top"))
```

# Raster Data

## 6) Import land surface temperature data with the terra package.

```{r, echo=FALSE, q6chunk7}
#Importing land surface temp data 

url <- "https://github.com/pjames-ucdavis/SPH215/raw/main/LST_med_ca.tif"

download.file(url, destfile = "LST_med_ca.tif", mode = "wb")

LST_raster = rast("LST_med_ca.tif")

#Summary of raster data 
LST_raster

#Check CRS
st_crs(LST_raster)
```

## 7) Make a map of land surface temperature across California

```{r q7chunk8}
tmap_mode("plot")

LST_map <-  tm_shape(LST_raster) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(),
            col.legend = tm_legend(outside = TRUE))
LST_map

# palette for plotting
palette_ndvi <- c("#BFBFBF","#DBDBDB","#FFFFE0","#FFFACC","#EDE8B5","#DED99C","#CCC782","#BDB86B","#B0C261","#A3CC59","#91BF52","#80B347","#70A340","#619636","#4F8A2E","#407D24","#306E1C","#216112","#0F540A","#004500")

LST_map <-  tm_shape(LST_raster) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = palette_ndvi),
            col.legend = tm_legend(title = "LST Median", outside = TRUE)) + tm_title(text = "LST Across CA",
           size = 1.25, 
           position = tm_pos_out("center","top"))
LST_map

```

## 8) Crop to these coordinates: ext(-122.8, -121.5, 37.5, 38.6) and make a map again.

```{r q8chunk9}

#Crop coordinates 
LST_crop <-crop(LST_raster, ext(-122.8, -121.5, 37.5, 38.6))

#Plot LST Raster Map w/ Cropped Coordinates
tmap_mode("plot")

LST_ca <- tm_shape(LST_crop) + tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = palette_ndvi), col.legend = tm_legend(title = "LST Median", outside = TRUE)) + tm_title(text = "LST Across CA",size = 1.25, position = tm_pos_out("center","top"))

LST_ca

```

# Overlay Cancer and Land surface temperature Data

## 9) Bring in our old CAdata ovarian cancer data set

```{r q9chunk11}
download.file("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pjames-ucdavis/SPH215/refs/heads/main/CAdata.rds", "CAdata.rds", mode = "wb")

CAdata <- readRDS("CAdata.rds")

ca_pts <- CAdata
ca_proj <- "+proj=lcc +lat_1=40 +lat_2=41.66666666666666 
             +lat_0=39.33333333333334 +lon_0=-122 +x_0=2000000 
             +y_0=500000.0000000002 +ellps=GRS80 
             +datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs"

ca_pts <- st_as_sf(CAdata, coords=c("X","Y"), crs=ca_proj)

```

## 10) Overlay a map of CAdata with the geocoded participant addresses in red on top of a map of the land surface temperature data for the whole state (not just what you cropped to).

```{r q10chunk12}
#Compare the data sets CRS
st_crs(ca_pts)
st_crs(LST_crop)

#Transform - Make them on the same projection 
ca_pts_proj <- st_transform(ca_pts,st_crs(LST_crop))

#Compare once more 
st_crs(ca_pts_proj)
st_crs(LST_crop)

#Overlay Maps - w/o cropped coordinates 
tmap_mode("plot")

lst_cancer_map <-  tm_shape(LST_raster) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(),
            col.legend = tm_legend(title = "CA Median LST", outside = TRUE)) +
  tm_shape(ca_pts_proj) +
  tm_dots(fill = "red", fill_alpha = 0.5, size = 0.3)

lst_cancer_map
```
